title: Seeds and Fruits in Year 6 Science: A Guide for Parents Who Do Not Speak German
audience: parents of Year 6 pupils at a Bavarian Gymnasium who do not speak German
hook: Your child has a subject called «Natur und Technik» and is growing cress on the windowsill for homework. This video explains what the subject is, what the seed topic teaches, and how to help, in about ten minutes.
keyTakeaway: The seed topic teaches three ways of thinking: which structure does which job, what a strategy costs and what it gains, and how an experiment with a control proves what caused what. Help with the thinking, not the German words.

youtube.description:
For parents who do not speak German and whose child attends Jahrgangsstufe 6 at a Gymnasium in Bavaria. What the subject Natur und Technik is, what the LehrplanPLUS expects in topic NT6 1.2 Samenpflanzen als Lebewesen, the core ideas in 3D pictures (parts of a seed, the fruit as dispersal unit, dispersal by wind and animals, bionics), the German terms with their English meaning, the cress experiment with a control for home, typical misconceptions and how the subject is assessed.

German terms in this video: Natur und Technik, Same, Frucht, Samenschale, Nährgewebe, Embryo, Keimwurzel, Keimspross, Keimblätter, Ausbreitung, Ahornfrucht, Klette, Bionik, Keimung, Hypothese, Variable, Kontrollversuch, Versuchsprotokoll, Ausläufer, Stegreifaufgabe.

The German version for parents (Eltern-Lektion) and the lesson for children (Lektion) are on this channel as well. Curriculum: LehrplanPLUS Gymnasium Bayern, Natur und Technik 6, Lernbereich 1.2.

chapters.title: What this is about
chapters.goal: You know what the subject is and what the curriculum expects in this topic.

scenes.onScreenTitle: Seeds and fruits: a guide for international parents
scenes.narration: Your child has a subject on the timetable called «Natur und Technik», nature and technology, and is growing cress on the windowsill for homework. This video is for parents who do not speak German. In about ten minutes you learn what the subject is, what the Bavarian curriculum expects in the topic on seed plants, which pictures carry the ideas, the German words your child will use, and how to help with a real experiment at home, even if you cannot read the worksheet.

bullets: Natur und Technik: the science subject in Years 5 to 7
Year 6: mostly biology, plus some informatics
Topic NT6 1.2 Samenpflanzen: seed plants, about 16 lessons
scenes.narration: «Natur und Technik», usually shortened to «NT», is the subject where science begins at a Bavarian Gymnasium. There is no separate biology, physics or chemistry yet; they come later. In Year six, «Jahrgangsstufe sechs», pupils aged eleven to twelve, the subject is mostly biology, with a smaller informatics part. The topic in this video is «Samenpflanzen als Lebewesen», seed plants as living things, planned for about sixteen lessons. It follows a first topic on the scientific method, which this topic puts to use.

bullets: Explain how seed and fruit structure serves their function
Compare dispersal strategies: costs and benefits
Bionics: compare plant parts with technical products
Draw conclusions from germination experiments
scenes.narration: The curriculum, the «LehrplanPLUS», lists four expectations for the first half of the topic. One: explain how the structure of fruits and seeds serves reproduction and dispersal, and weigh the costs and benefits of different dispersal strategies. Two: compare plant structures with technical products, which the curriculum calls «Bionik», bionics. Three: compare sexual and asexual reproduction by costs and benefits. Four: conclude from your own experiments how water, light, temperature and oxygen affect germination. The second half, plant parts and photosynthesis, is covered in another video.

chapters.title: The core ideas, in pictures
chapters.goal: You know the pictures your child uses for seed, fruit and dispersal, with the German words.

scenes.narration: One idea runs through the whole of school biology, and this topic introduces it: structure and function. Every part of a living thing has a shape, and the shape does a job. The question your child learns to ask is: why does it look like this, and what is it for? Three pictures carry that idea here: the seed cut open, the flying fruit, and the three ways a seed can travel. The captions on screen are German, as your child sees them in class.

scenes.onScreenTitle: Idea 1: the seed, a plant with packed lunch
scenes.narration: Idea one: the parts of a seed, «der Same». Cut lengthwise, three parts appear, and the curriculum names exactly these three. The seed coat, «die Samenschale», protects. The food store, «das Nährgewebe», feeds the young plant for its first days; in a bean it sits in the two thick seed leaves, «die Keimblätter». And the embryo, «der Embryo» or «der Keimling», is the tiny plant itself, with an embryonic root, «die Keimwurzel», and an embryonic shoot, «der Keimspross». The question is not what the parts are called, but what each part is for.

scenes.onScreenTitle: Idea 2: the fruit flies, and so does the rotor
scenes.narration: Idea two: the fruit, «die Frucht», is the seed's travel unit. The maple fruit, «die Ahornfrucht», carries its seed in a wing that spins as it falls, like a helicopter blade. Falling slowly gives the wind time to carry it away from the parent tree. This is where bionics comes in, «die Bionik», which the curriculum names explicitly: a helicopter rotor works on the same principle. Your child should be able to spot such a shared principle between a plant part and a machine and explain why it works in both.

scenes.onScreenTitle: Idea 3: three ways to travel, with costs
scenes.narration: Idea three: dispersal, «die Ausbreitung», compared by costs and benefits. Wind: the dandelion makes very many light fruits with little parachutes; most land badly, some travel far. Animals that eat: the cherry invests in sweet flesh and gets targeted transport, with fertiliser on arrival. Animals that carry: the burr, «die Klette», hooks into fur and pays nothing in flesh. The curriculum asks for exactly this comparison: what does a strategy cost the plant, and what does it gain?

chapters.title: The words your child brings home
chapters.goal: You recognise the German terms and know what they mean.

scenes.narration: Here are the words in one place, in three groups: the words for the seed and for sprouting, the words for travelling and bionics, and the words for the experiment, which matter beyond this topic because they return in every science lesson for years. You do not need to pronounce them. You need to recognise them when your child says them or when they appear on a worksheet.

bullets: Same = seed; Frucht = fruit; Samenschale = seed coat
Nährgewebe = food store; Embryo, Keimling = embryo
Keimwurzel, Keimspross = embryonic root and shoot
Keimung = germination; Mutterpflanze = parent plant
scenes.narration: The seed is «der Same», plural «die Samen»; do not confuse it with «der Samen», which also means seed. The fruit is «die Frucht». The coat is «die Samenschale», the store «das Nährgewebe», the embryo «der Embryo» or «der Keimling». Its root is «die Keimwurzel», its shoot «der Keimspross». Sprouting is «die Keimung», and the verb is «keimen». The plant the seed comes from is «die Mutterpflanze», literally the mother plant. Most of these are built from small words: «Keim» means germ or sprout, and it starts half of them.

bullets: Ausbreitung = dispersal; Bionik = bionics
Ahornfrucht = maple fruit; Klette = burr
Hypothese, Variable, Kontrollversuch = hypothesis, variable, control
Versuchsprotokoll = experiment record
scenes.narration: Travelling is «die Ausbreitung», dispersal. «Die Bionik» is bionics, technology inspired by nature. The maple fruit is «die Ahornfrucht», the burr «die Klette», and the Velcro it inspired is «der Klettverschluss». Then the experiment words, which your child will use for years: «die Hypothese», the hypothesis, «die Variable», the one thing you change, «die Konstanten», what stays the same, «der Kontrollversuch», the control experiment, and «das Versuchsprotokoll», the written record of the experiment. These last five are the most valuable words in the whole topic.

scenes.question: Your child says: "Das ist mein Kontrollversuch." and points at a dish of cress with no water. What is the dish for?
scenes.hint: Think about what you would not know without it.
scenes.narration: A quick check for you. Your child has two dishes of cress on the windowsill, points at the dry one and says: «Das ist mein Kontrollversuch». What is that dish for, and why does the experiment need it? Take a moment. Think about what you would not know if there were only the watered dish.

bullets: Kontrollversuch = the control: everything the same but the variable
Without it you cannot tell what caused the result
Cress grows only in the wet dish: water was the cause
scenes.narration: The dry dish is the control, «der Kontrollversuch». It is treated exactly like the other dish, same seeds, same place, same warmth, except for the one thing being tested, the water. If only the watered dish sprouts, the water was the cause. Without the control, cress sprouting in the watered dish would prove nothing; maybe it would have sprouted dry as well. This is the single most important idea in the scientific method your child is learning, and it is worth a conversation at the windowsill.

chapters.title: The experiment at home
chapters.goal: You can support the germination experiment with a variable, constants and a control, without German.

scenes.narration: The most useful thing you can do at home is the experiment itself. The curriculum wants children to conclude from their own experiments how water, light, temperature and oxygen affect germination, guided by a hypothesis. That sounds big, but cress, cotton wool and two dishes do it in a week. You need no German for this: the method is the same in every language, and your child supplies the German words.

scenes.onScreenTitle: The cress experiment, step by step
bullets: Hypothesis: cress needs water to germinate
Two dishes, same seeds, same warm bright place
Variable: only one dish is watered
After three days: count, note, conclude
scenes.narration: Step one: your child writes down a hypothesis, «die Hypothese»: cress needs water to germinate. Step two: two dishes with cotton wool, the same number of seeds, the same warm, bright place. Step three: only one dish is watered. That single difference is the variable; everything kept the same are the constants; the dry dish is the control. Step four: after three days, count how many seeds have sprouted in each dish and write a short record: question, hypothesis, set-up, observation, conclusion. That record is the «Versuchsprotokoll» the teacher expects.

scenes.onScreenTitle: Questions you can ask, in any language
bullets: What did you change, and what did you keep the same?
What is the second dish for?
What if you changed two things at once?
Was your hypothesis right? How can you tell?
scenes.narration: You do not have to explain anything; you can ask. What did you change, and what did you keep the same? What is the second dish for? What would you not know without it? What would happen if you changed water and light at the same time? Then you could not tell which one caused the result, and that insight is the heart of the method. Finally: was your hypothesis right, and how can you tell? A child who can answer these in any language has understood the method, not just the cress.

bullets: Temperature: one dish in the fridge
Light: one dish under a cardboard box
Air: seeds fully under water
Always one variable at a time
scenes.narration: Once the first experiment has worked, the other factors in the curriculum follow the same pattern. Temperature: one dish in the fridge, one in the room. Light: one dish under a cardboard box. Oxygen: seeds fully under water instead of on damp cotton wool. Always one variable at a time, everything else the same. The light experiment holds a surprise worth discussing: many seeds germinate in the dark. Plants need light mainly afterwards, to grow, which is why the shoot races upwards.

chapters.title: Misconceptions, assessment, and what comes next
chapters.goal: You know the typical misconceptions, how the subject is assessed, and which topics follow.

scenes.narration: Three things parents often ask. Which wrong ideas are common, and how do you spot them? How is this subject assessed, since it works differently from maths and German? And what else is in this topic? The misconceptions are stubborn because they come from everyday life. The assessment is lighter than in the main subjects. And the second half of the topic is harder than the first.

bullets: Fruit and seed are the same: no, the fruit contains the seed
All seeds need light to germinate: no, many sprout in the dark
A seed is dead: no, it rests and waits for conditions
The seedling eats soil: no, it lives on its store
scenes.narration: Four misconceptions that appear in many classes. One: fruit and seed are the same thing. The fruit is the packaging, the seed is inside; a cherry stone and an apple pip make this clear. Two: all seeds need light to germinate. Many sprout in the dark underground; light is needed afterwards, for growing. Three: a seed is dead. It is resting and waiting for water, warmth and air. Four: the seedling feeds on soil. For its first days it lives on the store inside the seed, and later on light, water and carbon dioxide. Each of these is corrected by a picture or an experiment, not by a rule.

scenes.onScreenTitle: How this subject is usually assessed
bullets: Usually no big written tests (Schulaufgaben) in this subject
Short tests, participation, experiment records, presentations
Typical tasks: label a seed, justify a strategy, evaluate an experiment
Details are the teacher's decision
scenes.narration: In Year six, «Natur und Technik» is usually one of the subjects without the big written tests called «Schulaufgaben». Grades come from smaller pieces: short unannounced tests, «Stegreifaufgaben», oral participation, experiment records and sometimes presentations. Typical tasks in this topic: label a seed in section, justify the dispersal strategy of a given fruit, compare costs and benefits, evaluate a germination experiment and explain the control. How exactly your child's school handles this is the teacher's decision; the exercise book and the experiment records show it.

scenes.onScreenTitle: What comes next in this topic
bullets: Root, stem and leaf: what each plant part does
Photosynthesis and respiration: matter and energy
Why it matters: food, materials, fossil fuels
Plants respond: towards light, opening flowers
scenes.narration: The second half of the topic is more demanding. First the jobs of the plant parts: root, stem and leaf, «Wurzel», «Sprossachse» and «Blatt». Then photosynthesis and respiration, «Photosynthese» and «Zellatmung», simplified to the level of particles, with the idea of converting matter and energy: the plant builds sugar from water and carbon dioxide using light. From that follows why plants matter for food, renewable materials and fossil fuels. Finally, plants respond to their surroundings: they grow towards light and open and close their flowers. Those get their own videos.

In short: this topic teaches three ways of thinking. Structure and function: what is each part of the seed and the fruit for? Costs and benefits: what does a plant invest in its dispersal, and what does it gain? And the experiment with a control: what really caused the result? Ask about these three things at home, grow cress with a «Kontrollversuch», and let your child explain the record to you in any language. The German version of this guide and the lesson for children are on this channel. Subscribe for the next topic.
